$comment: One row per requirement in PRD.md, naming the evidence that proves it. Generated by hand, enforced by `npm run check:fr-evidence` (scripts/check-fr-evidence.mjs), which fails if an id or title drifts from PRD.md, if a citation points at a file that does not exist, if a browser anchor is not defined by scripts/browser-matrix.mjs, or if a row claims more than it can show. PRD.md is the target and never records status; this file is the status and never restates the target — so no row here repeats requirement text, only cites it.

statesMeaning.met: every clause of the requirement is implemented, tested, documented and guarded
statesMeaning.partial: built, but at least one named clause is not — see gaps
statesMeaning.absent: the clause exists in PRD.md and nothing in the package satisfies it

FR-01.title: Input Flexibility
gaps: a relative URL with no base URL is not refused — resolveSourceUrl returns the input unchanged
unsupported schemes are refused only by accident: javascript: is caught by the bare-name rule, while any scheme containing a slash (chrome://) classifies as a url
FR-01.note: Every input kind and all four refusal reasons exist and are tested; the base-URL refusal and the scheme allowlist are clause-level holes rather than missing features.

FR-02.title: Worker Configuration
gaps: two simultaneous viewers with conflicting worker URLs are not detected, and there is no PdfError with the CONFIGURATION_ERROR code naming both origins
FR-02.note: Host URL, imported asset, CDN URL, probe-before-write and the no-worker fallback are each measured; only the conflict clause is unbuilt, and it depends on the error contract task.

FR-03.title: Password Protection
FR-03.acceptanceWaiver: The encrypted load, the parked promise and the observable re-prompt are proven against the real engine in Node on playground/fixtures/encrypted-sample.pdf; the browser harness has no password check, and the prompt's rendering is covered by the a11y audit instead.

FR-04.title: Cancellation Safety
gaps: the AbortSignal reason is not preserved: abortError() fabricates a fresh Error with name AbortError and no call site reads signal.reason
FR-04.note: Cancellation is identified by name, distinguished from failure and never reaches onError; only the preserve-the-reason clause is unmet.

FR-06.title: Responsive Zoom Modes
gaps: no test asserts the text layer is updated in place on a zoom step: TextLayer.update is an empty mock, so the clause rests on code plus one browser measurement
FR-06.note: Range, fit modes and automatic fit are implemented and tested, and the structure layer's no-rebuild clause is guarded; the text-layer half of the same clause is not.

FR-08.title: Page Layouts
gaps: rows are keyed by their first index, so a page that stops being a row head (continuous to spread drops keys 2, 4, ...) unmounts and remounts — the no-remount clause fails and nothing tests it
FR-08.note: Grouping lives in the virtualizer and repaint-on-fit-movement was measured, but the identity of a row across a layout switch is exactly what the current key destroys.

FR-09.title: Rotation
gaps: no test asserts the overlay layers stay registered to the painted page after a rotation; only browser checks observe it, and edge-cases.test.ts proves the viewport maths, not the layer
FR-09.note: Per-page and document rotation work and every layer re-runs on rotation; the assertion that it registered correctly is missing.

FR-10.title: Outline
gaps: a click resolves to a page but not to a position: OutlineEntry carries pageIndex only and scrollToPage goes to the row top, discarding the destination's Y and zoom
FR-10.note: Recursive parsing, named destinations, object-reference translation and a valid nested ARIA tree are all met and axe-audited; the destination's position is dropped on the floor.

FR-11.title: Thumbnails
gaps: no jsdom test exists for PdfThumbnail or ThumbnailList, so nothing in CI fails if the card stops using the measured width, the pixel ratio or the visible-range tracking
FR-11.note: The behaviour is implemented as written and proven in a browser only. A requirement guarded by a browser check that has never run outside Chromium is the weakest evidence in this register.

FR-13.title: Text Indexing
gaps: the bounded-interval yield exists only in extractAllText, which no code in src/ calls; the path the shell actually indexes through has no timed yield and relies on each await being a worker round trip
no test observes the yield at all
FR-13.note: Progress reporting and the per-document index are met and tested. The clause about never blocking interaction is satisfied by the engine's round trips, not by the design the requirement describes.

FR-16.title: AcroForm Support
FR-16.acceptanceWaiver: The widgets are constructed by pdf.js's own AnnotationLayer, so the clause is proven by rendering the form fixture and asserting the control set in jsdom; no browser check adds evidence the unit tests do not already carry.

FR-17.title: Form Data Sync
FR-17.acceptanceWaiver: Two-way binding, plain-object serialisation, reset and dirty tracking are pure data operations asserted on the AcroForm fixture; the browser harness has no form-fill check and one would repeat the unit evidence.

FR-18.title: Annotations: View
gaps: the annotation view half is built, but the withdrawal half is not: root and /headless still export InkLayer, usePdfInk, INK_COLORS, INK_WIDTHS and the stroke helpers
ViewerController instantiates usePdfInk unconditionally, so the shell renders a working pen with no feature loaded
src/lib/features.ts bakes transient core ink into the core feature contract
FR-18.note: State is absent because the requirement now names a removal, and that removal has not happened: ink.test.ts tests the surface that is meant to go away (task #200). Verified against the published artifact rather than inferred — usePdfInk, InkLayer, INK_COLORS, INK_WIDTHS, drawInkStrokes, simplifyPoints and InkStroke all appear in dist/index.d.ts of pdfjs-react-reader@0.1.2 on npm, so this is a public-API removal, not an internal one.

FR-19.title: High-Fidelity Printing
gaps: print feeds core transient inkStrokesForPage into the sheet, so unpersisted core drawing travels — the clause says there is no transient core drawing capability (depends on FR-18)
no acceptance evidence: the print path has never been opened in a browser by the matrix
FR-19.note: Budget-driven resolution, the refusal that names the page count, form values, persisted marks and the known-broken platform report are all built and planned by the unit tests.

FR-20.title: Document Download
FR-20.acceptanceWaiver: Download is a Blob and an object-URL lifecycle; jsdom asserts the branch taken and the filename, and a browser check would observe the same bytes the unit tests already compare.

FR-21.title: Opt-In Feature Registration
gaps: no declared dependency list, no duplicate-id handling and no cycle detection, so the deterministic-failure clause is unbuilt (task #197)
the feature value declares no stylesheet entries
FR-21.note: The shell imports no feature statically and runners are keyed by feature id with the index-key counterfactual tested; the §3.7 validation half is missing.

FR-22.title: Per-Feature Stylesheets
gaps: the core stylesheet carries all the ink chrome (.pjsr-ink rules) while annotate.css carries none, so the core sheet does hold rules for a capability the application did not request
no gate asserts CSS purity: check-size.mjs asserts JavaScript markers only
FR-22.note: One stylesheet per tier is published and imported explicitly. The clause that the core sheet carries no rules for unrequested features fails today because of the core ink the register already flags.

FR-24.title: Optional-Content Layers
FR-24.acceptanceWaiver: The shared-instance clause is impossible to satisfy as literally written — pdf.js builds a new config per call — so the code passes one owned instance to both the panel and every render, and the impossibility is measured and documented in the module rather than re-proved in a browser.

FR-25.title: Embedded Files
gaps: a file carried by an annotation rather than named in the name tree is listed by accident: this repo enumerates getAttachments() and relies on pdf.js including FileAttachment annotations
playground/fixtures/attachments-ocg-sample.pdf carries exactly such a file and is wired into no test
FR-25.note: Descriptions, per-file reads and saving annotation-held files work; the listing clause depends on the engine rather than on an assertion.

FR-27.title: Search Depth
gaps: the 256 UTF-16 code-unit ceiling does not exist: planFind never checks length, so an over-long pattern is indistinguishable from a valid one (task #199)
FR-27.note: AND-per-page, literal escaping, raw regex, a pattern error rather than zero matches, per-page counts and cancellation are all met; the ceiling is the one clause with no code.

FR-28.title: Composed Shell, Labels, Events, Locales & Shell Affordances

FR-29.title: Annotation Authoring
FR-29.acceptanceWaiver: Editors surviving scroll-out, rotation and zoom was browser-verified during 0.6 and the persistence half is asserted by writing and re-opening real files; the matrix has no annotate check and adding one repeats the engine-level evidence.

FR-30.title: Page Authoring
FR-30.acceptanceWaiver: Reorder, delete, rotate, extract and split are asserted by writing real files and re-opening them in jsdom, which is the same byte-level evidence a browser pass would produce at higher cost.

FR-31.title: True Flattening
FR-31.acceptanceWaiver: Flattening is asserted on written files by re-reading them, including the missing-appearance case that made unsigned forms throw; there is nothing a browser check would see that the bytes do not already show.

FR-32.title: Visual Signing
FR-32.acceptanceWaiver: A written mark painting in both file-borne and in-session documents was browser-verified during the signing spike and recorded in the changelog; the matrix carries no signing check yet, which is tracked rather than claimed here.
FR-32.note: Marks are written into every widget box a field declares, in page coordinates, and the already-signed refusal is now a thrown `ALREADY_SIGNED` that fails the whole call before anything is written, rather than a name in a `refused` list shared with fields that do not exist: three of four boxes signed still reads as a signed document, and nothing in it says which one is missing. The built-in pad disables those rows, so the throw is what a programmatic caller meets.

FR-33.title: XFA Display, Save Refused
gaps: the refusal names no reason to the host: usePdfDownload silently falls back to the loaded bytes, so a reader gets a file without their edits and is told nothing
FR-33.note: XfaLayer renders, marks wrap its text runs and thumbnails draw the tree, and a save of a pure-XFA document is refused rather than attempted — the refusal itself is the measured pdf.js behaviour, whose commit call rejects. What is missing is the reason reaching anyone: usePdfDownload falls back to the loaded bytes silently, so the reader gets a file without their edits and nothing says so. The clause is W2's (#204), where it moved from W1's row at W1's close; and whatever carries it belongs on FR-54's coded error surface rather than in a message, since the contract now exists.

FR-34.title: Network Contract
FR-34.acceptanceWaiver: Bearer, cookie and signed-URL loading was proven by hand against scripts/auth-server.mjs, a dev-only server; the browser matrix refuses the network by design, so its evidence would be a CDN assertion, not an auth one.

FR-35.title: Bounded Retries
gaps: defaults are 250 ms initial and 5 s maximum against the locked 1 s and 30 s

the last attempt is never reported: the throw precedes the report call, and retry.test.tsx asserts one wait between two attempts and not after the last, so the clause is currently guarded in the wrong direction
the backoff is an un-cancellable setTimeout with cancellation checked after it resumes, so an abort leaves a timer running for the remainder of the delay
FR-35.note: Attempt count, the 408/425/429 and 5xx status set, 401 and 403 never retried, and full jitter are all met and tested; the three clauses §7's rewrite turned into obligations are not (task #199).

FR-36.title: Cancellation Tokens
gaps: every writer pass is not covered: src/edit.tsx calls arrangePages, flattenBytes, signFields and findSignatureFields with no WriteOptions, so the signal only reaches the writer through /merge
download checks the signal only between the byte await and the write, so an already-aborted download still does the work — its own test names this the honest boundary
the page-proxy fetch sets a cancelled flag and still issues doc.getPage(), which is cancellation by discarding rather than by doing no work
FR-36.note: All nine operations accept a signal and the superseded-load path never reaches an error handler, which is the hard half; the two exceptions are documented rather than wished away.

FR-37.title: Published State Models
FR-37.note: Both models are produced, not merely declared. `cancelled` is what a host that aborts a load observes — the earlier assertion that an aborted load lands on `destroyed` was a departure from §3.5 and is gone, with `destroyed` kept for the unmount and the superseded load, where there is nobody left to tell — and `retryPage(page)` on the handle plus `retryToken` on `PdfPage` publish the re-queue §3.5 promises instead of leaving it inside the virtualizer. The fields (`doc`, `isReady`, `error`) are read off the state, so they still cannot disagree with it.
FR-37.acceptanceWaiver: Both unions are produced by components under test rather than declared and unreachable: the document path is driven through a host `AbortSignal` and a password prompt in jsdom, and the page path through fake render tasks whose settle and failure the test controls. What a browser would add — real scroll-out timing — is covered as behaviour by FR-04’s checks, not as a state the model can only show on a device.

FR-38.title: Source Utilities
FR-38.acceptanceWaiver: base64ToBytes and classifySource are pure functions over strings; the browser cannot add evidence about a heuristic that never touches the DOM, and both barrels export them so the packaging check covers reachability.

FR-39.title: Incremental, Viewport-Prioritised Indexing
gaps: re-indexing after a page edit invalidates only what changed, but what it re-reads is the content stream, which cannot see annotationStorage — so a form or ink edit never becomes searchable. This is a pdf.js limit rather than an omission, and the module says so at usePdfSearch.ts:104-115
the test that covers this is titled as though a typed form field were re-found, which overstates what it proves
FR-39.note: Viewport-first order, the outward walk and the provisional channel (complete:false making total and counts floors) are met and measured; the invalidation clause satisfies its words and not its intent.

FR-40.title: Injectable External Index
FR-40.acceptanceWaiver: Parity is proven on real fixtures by round-tripping the published shape through JSON and matching offsets; no browser surface is involved, since the host supplies the index and the shell only reads matches.

FR-41.title: Dual Module Output
gaps: engines.node is >=20 while the contract floor is >=22.13.0 and forbids Node 20 and 22.0–22.12
the packaging matrix tests 20.9, 20 and 22 with no 22.13 pin, so it measures runtimes the contract excludes
tarball-check treats ERR_REQUIRE_ESM as a pass on any version, so cannot-be-required fails the job only if the runner happens to be new enough
FR-41.note: Fifteen paths × four files with matching name lists between formats, proven from the packed artifact; the Node floor that makes CJS loadable at all is stated in the PRD and contradicted by package.json (task #202).

FR-42.title: Document Merge
FR-42.acceptanceWaiver: Page-level selection and order preview are asserted against real files written and re-read in Node; the playground mounts MergeDemo in place of the viewer, so there is deliberately no in-viewer acceptance path to claim.

FR-43.title: Structure-Tree Integration
gaps: the clause is what a screen reader hears, and no environment here proves it: no browser check reads the structure tree and the VoiceOver/Safari pairing has no runner
the annotation and editor layers both receive the structure instance, which is asserted, but that the widget is announced with its owning node is not
FR-43.note: Handing the builder to both layers and degrading an untagged document to the plain text layer are built and tested against a real tagged fixture; the announcement half of the requirement is the same unbuilt screen-reader evidence FR-45 names.

FR-44.title: High Contrast & Forced Colours
gaps: the browser check asserts the page-slot outline and shadow only, never the second channels or focus visibility, and jsdom cannot resolve colour at all
FR-44.note: Tokens re-pointed at system colours, shadows turned into outlines and the four forced-color-adjust: none cases are each justified in the stylesheet; the proof that a reader sees the difference is thinner than the implementation.

FR-45.title: WCAG 2.2 AA Conformance
gaps: the required NVDA+Firefox, JAWS+Chromium and VoiceOver+Safari pass has no environment, no job, no operator log and no dated record
44 px targets and contrast are asserted as CSS declarations, not measured: jsdom performs no layout
axe runs against a rule set the audit test itself declares incomplete
FR-45.note: Automated axe, DOM structure, instance-scoped keys, generated ids, reduced motion and keyboard paging are all covered by checks that fail when they regress; what is missing is the human and platform-specific evidence the requirement says an automated audit cannot replace.

FR-46.title: SSR-Safe Module Graph
gaps: the requirement says the test covers the published tarball, and the file says plainly that dist/ is not touched: the tarball half lives in check:tarball, which is outside verify, needs the network, and has never run on a clean runner
FR-46.note: Every documented entry imports under bare Node without a DOM and the entry list is read from package.json rather than typed out, so a new subpath cannot escape the check; only the artifact-under-test claim is overstated.

FR-48.title: Browser & Engine Verification Matrices
gaps: Firefox and WebKit cannot start on the development host, so only Chromium rows carry evidence and the CI job that would cover the other two has never run
the browser job installs Playwright's current defaults rather than the pinned per-floor environments §8's execution policy requires
the engine matrix has no latest-supported-6.x row, and the React matrix has no minimum-supported-patch row per major
verify still runs Node 20 against an 22.13.0 floor, and no Edge, macOS Safari, iOS or Android job exists
FR-48.note: Thirteen checks × three engines × two profiles are written and the harness classifies a launch failure as unverified rather than passed, which is the honest part; the coverage itself is one engine and one never-run job.

FR-49.title: Benchmark Fixture Suite
gaps: profiles C (vector-heavy) and D (low-memory harness) have no committed fixture
the measurement record omits the machine model, browser version, fixture hash and p99 that §6 requires, and .spike/ is gitignored so no record is committed at all
the in-script profile C target restates a cold-page number §6 does not give
the CI benchmark step has never run remotely
FR-49.note: Profiles A and B are built, generated by committed scripts, and separated into bars that fail the run and measures that never do; the record §6 demands a measurement carry does not exist yet.

FR-50.title: Published API Maturity
gaps: the check is the last step of npm run verify, which no CI job calls, so an untagged export fails locally and passes CI
FR-50.note: All 315 published names are tagged with the four §5.5 states and every rule the requirement promises is implemented and self-tested; only the enforcement location is wrong.

FR-51.title: Edge-Case Suite
gaps: the over-large page row asserts canvas arithmetic ceilings rather than what the engine reports for a page that size, because no oversize fixture exists (task #195)
FR-51.note: Four of six shapes run against the real engine, two are cited with a stated reason, and three guards make the table evidence rather than prose; the sixth row is computed, and says so.

FR-52.title: Public API & Export Contract
gaps: npm run check:examples does not exist, so the compile rule the PRD's own reading guide states is unenforced (task #201)
no assertion makes internal modules unreachable or forbids a /types entry appearing
the packaging job that proves both formats from the packed artifact has never run

the /edit, /merge, /features/*, per-feature CSS and /locales/* entries this row classifies as public have never been published: the surface consumers have actually had is the four subpaths in pdfjs-react-reader@0.1.2 — '.', './headless', './styles.css', './package.json' — ESM only
FR-52.note: Twenty-five published subpaths with complete declarations and no wildcards, checked against the built output; the example-compile half of the contract has no mechanism. The published-baseline fact matters twice over: nothing in this row can be a breaking change, because no consumer has ever resolved those paths, and FR-50's stable/experimental split should be derived from them rather than from a local commit.

FR-53.title: Dependency & Engine Contract
gaps: nothing forbids the root or /headless entry from importing the writer in future — it holds today by arrangement, not by assertion
no check enforces the no-undeclared-runtime-dependency rule
engines.node is >=20 while the contract floor is 22.13.0 (task #202)
FR-53.note: Peer ranges, the optional writer peer and a consumer that installs the packed artifact all exist and are tested; the two promises that prevent future drift are not yet asserted.

FR-54.title: Stable Error & Cancellation Contract
FR-54.acceptanceWaiver: Every code is produced on a path the node and dom harnesses already run — a refused source, a 401, a dismissed password prompt, a cancelled load, render, index and writer pass, a print job over the memory budget, a plan naming a page that is not there — and each is asserted by its own test. No row of the browser matrix injects a failure today, so browser evidence here would be a claim rather than a record; the matrix is about engines and environments, not about error vocabulary.
FR-54.note: The contract is §3.6 as a published interface: `PdfError` with the eighteen `PDF_ERROR_CODES`, three cancellation codes, `details` carrying numbers rather than prose, and the engine error preserved as `cause`. Every consumer-visible failure path routes through it — load, page render, overlay layers, text indexing, print, download, merge, the writer, source refusals, the feature and viewer context guards, and Trusted Types configuration. Two things worth recording while they are fresh. (1) `isPdfError` matches the *shape* (a code from the list, beside a message) and never the class name, because `abortError()` returns a `PdfError` that keeps `name: "AbortError"` — every cancellation filter here and in hosts reads that name, so renaming it would put cancelled renders into error handlers, and a guard on the name would call an abort a non-error. (2) `RENDER_CANCELLED` and `UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE` are produced by mapping the engine’s own exceptions through `toPdfError`; a render this package cancels never becomes an error object at all, which is FR-04 working rather than a missing throw site.

FR-55.title: Worker & Source Security Contract
gaps: conflicting worker configurations across simultaneous viewers are not detected, so one worker per realm is a convention rather than an enforced contract
FR-55.note: allowedSources, scripting disabled at the layer, the Trusted Types policy and honest redirect scoping are built. The credential clauses §3.6 adds are now both held and asserted: a refusal names only the origin through `describeOrigin`, and the test that refuses a pre-signed source asserts the token *and* the path are absent from the message. Detecting two viewers with different worker URLs is the remaining half (task #198).

FR-56.title: Feature Lifecycle Contract
gaps: six of §3.7's eight obligations are absent: dependency declaration, cleanup contract, stylesheet declaration, duplicate-id validation, missing-dependency and cycle validation, dependency-before-dependent ordering
none of the three registration failures has a test, which §3.7 states explicitly
FR-56.note: Stable ids, identity-keyed runners and merged page props are real; the lifecycle half of the contract is the target §3.7 was written to make checkable (task #197).

FR-57.title: Runtime Resource Budget Contract
gaps: there is no platform probe: canvas safety is chosen from user-agent and platform labels, and the module header documents rejecting a boot-time probe as a design decision §6.1 now reverses
a host-supplied budget replaces the computed ceiling rather than constraining it
no minimum-render-scale floor exists and nothing refuses a page with RESOURCE_LIMIT
FR-57.note: The four canonical values are single-sourced, tested, read by the benchmark rather than copied, and the viewport-derived term is implemented — but the §6.1 combination rule and its detection clause are unwritten (task #198).

FR-58.title: Release Evidence & Consumer Verification
gaps: no release candidate has ever been built and tested on a clean runner from a packed artifact — the packaging, consumer and browser jobs exist but have never executed
the real-device pass and the three screen-reader pairings have no environment, no schedule and no artifact
the 0.1.2 to 1.0.0 upgrade path is not exercised by anything
benchmark and accessibility evidence is printed to a console and a gitignored directory rather than produced as a committed, reproducible record
FR-58.note: This is the gate §9 stands on and the one requirement whose evidence cannot be manufactured locally: the scripts to run it exist, the environments to certify it do not (tasks #202, #194).
